subject: Cloud marketplace rate slab proposal & next actions
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Chris Norton <chris.norton@skylineclinical.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud marketplace rate slab proposal & next actions

Hi Chris —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, putting a short summary here so we have alignment before we start drafting the private offer: 

Key asks / facts you shared
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~120M tokens/month, with seasonal spikes to ~250M for a new product launch window.
- Target budget range: $18k–$30k/month in the first year (targeting ~$24k/mo ideally).
- Desired commercial: unit economics target ~ $20–$25 / 1M tokens for base generation model; ability to tier down for embedding-heavy workloads.
- Procurement note: Skyline prefers private offers via the AWS marketplace (primary), but is evaluating GCP marketplace for redundancy. Azure not in scope for initial rollout.

Open items we need from Skyline to map to marketplace SKUs/private-offer bands:
1) Purchase vehicle — will this be a single annual commit or quarterly reserved spend? (this affects whether we set a flat PPU or commit-tiered discounts)
2) A definitive list of expected peak months (so we can size burst capacity and recommend a burst/commit split)
3) Confirmation whether embeddings vs. generation split is ~60/40 (as discussed) or different.

Next steps from Redwood (we'll action once we have the above):
- Draft a marketplace private-offer proposal with 3 slabed unit prices (commit tiers) and a fallback hosted API price for overages. (Deliverable: worksheet + recommended PPU per tier) — owner: Markus, ETA: 48 hours.
- Produce a short procurement checklist and DocuSign-ready order form to accelerate acceptance — owner: Laura, ETA: 72 hours.
- Technical note: Karthik will validate the model variants for AWS marketplace packaging and call out any architecture restrictions for multi-region fallbacks.

I've attached a starter worksheet (redwood-marketplace-rate-slabs.xlsx) with baseline calculations and two example slab structures. Markus / Karthik — I flagged where we should insert kernel/quantization assumptions for the PPU reconciliation.

Chris — if that reads correctly, reply with the procurement answers and I’ll push a private-offer draft for your procurement team to review. If anything above is off, correct in-line.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: redwood-marketplace-rate-slabs.xlsx, ma-draft-redlines.docx
From: Chris Norton <chris.norton@skylineclinical.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace rate slab proposal & next actions

Laura —

Thanks for the quick recap. All accurate from our side with two clarifications: 
1) Procurement will prefer an annual commit but needs a quarterly invoicing cadence if possible (accounting constraint). So draft should show annual committed units with quarterly invoicing/measurement.
2) Embeddings will run heavier than I initially said — updated split is roughly 70% embeddings / 30% generation (longer vectors, more calls). That should influence the recommended slab pricing.

Attached is a short internal budget extract (skyline-budget-range-2027.pdf) that shows the funding band we were authorized to pursue for this initiative — the $18k–$30k/month figure is still the right north star.

Happy for Markus to draft the pricing bands, and procurement@skylineclinical.com is on copy to coordinate the DocuSign path.

Cheers,
Chris
Director, Data Platforms
Skyline Clinical
chris.norton@skylineclinical.com

Chris / Laura —

Thanks — updated assumptions noted (70/30 embeddings/generation). Quick technical-commercial note before I produce the slab worksheet: 

- Marketplace SKU mapping constraints: AWS private offers require a mapping to a specific marketplace product SKU (we typically create three SKUs representing Commit Tier A/B/C). Each SKU must have an associated per-unit price and a billing unit (we map tokens -> 1M-token units). For GCP we can mirror slabs but the private offer flows are different (commit -> discounts applied at billing).
- Recommendation: Build slabs that optimize for your steady state (120M/mo) but include a launch-burst slab that gives deeper unit discounts for the first 3 months up to 250M tokens. That keeps unit $/1M attractive during the high-adoption window while protecting Redwood economics outside the window.
- Edge case: If embeddings dominate (as now expected), we should include an embeddings-specific SKU at ~40–50% of generation PPU because embeddings are cheaper computationally per token in your workload. I will call out a suggested mapping in the workbook.

Deliverables (per Laura's note):
- redwood-marketplace-rate-slabs.xlsx: three slab templates with suggested AWS/GCP price parity and an embedding-specific SKU option.
- ma-draft-redlines.docx: procurement language that supports annual committed units with quarterly invoicing and an overage calculation.

I’ll push the XLSX up to the Drive link and attach a local copy here. Expect the draft in the next 6 business hours.

—Markus
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
